stem: Republic Act No. 6713 is also known as the:
choices: Ease of Doing Business and Efficient Government Service Delivery Act
Civil Service Law on the Discipline of Public Officials and Employees
Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees
Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act for Public Officers and Employees
explanation: Section 1 of RA 6713 names it the "Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees." The Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act is RA 3019, and the Ease of Doing Business Act is RA 11032.
quote: This Act shall be known as the "Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees."

stem: Under RA 6713, public officials and employees shall lead modest lives and uphold:
choices: the interest of their political party
loyalty to their superiors above all
explanation: The declaration of policy in Section 2 requires public officials and employees to lead modest lives and uphold public interest over personal interest.
quote: lead modest lives, and uphold public interest over personal interest

stem: Under RA 6713, the term "public officials" includes employees who are:
choices: occupying positions at or above a minimum salary grade set by law
permanent or temporary, provided they receive at least the minimum wage
permanent and in the career service, receiving regular compensation
permanent or temporary, whether or not they receive compensation
explanation: Section 3(b) covers elective and appointive officials and employees, permanent or temporary, career or non-career, including military and police personnel, whether or not they receive compensation, regardless of amount.
quote: permanent or temporary, whether in the career or non-career service, including military and police personnel, whether or not they receive compensation, regardless of amount

stem: Under RA 6713, which of the following is NOT considered a "gift"?
choices: A free trip offered by a contractor with a pending bid
A simulated sale in favor of the official
An unsolicited gift of nominal value not given in exchange for a favor
Cash given in anticipation of a favor
explanation: Section 3(c) excludes an unsolicited gift of nominal or insignificant value not given in anticipation of, or in exchange for, a favor.
quote: It shall not include an unsolicited gift of nominal or insignificant value not given in anticipation of, or in exchange for, a favor from a public official or employee.

stem: For purposes of RA 6713, the "family" of a public official or employee means their:
choices: relatives within the fourth civil degree
spouse and unmarried children under eighteen years of age
explanation: Section 3(g) defines the family of public officials or employees as their spouses and unmarried children under eighteen (18) years of age.
quote: "Family of public officials or employees" means their spouses and unmarried children under eighteen (18) years of age.

stem: Under RA 6713, "relatives" refers to persons related to a public official within what degree of consanguinity or affinity?
explanation: Section 3(k) defines relatives as persons related within the fourth civil degree of consanguinity or affinity, including bilas, inso and balae.
quote: within the fourth civil degree of consanguinity or affinity, including bilas, inso and balae

stem: Under RA 6713, a "conflict of interest" arises when an official's interest in a private corporation or business:
choices: earns more income than the salary the official receives from the government
is registered under the name of the official's spouse or minor children
is located outside the Philippines and not taxed by the government
may be opposed to or affected by the faithful performance of official duty
explanation: Section 3(i) says conflict of interest arises when the interest of the corporation or business, or the official's rights or duties in it, may be opposed to or affected by the faithful performance of official duty.
quote: may be opposed to or affected by the faithful performance of official duty

stem: "Divestment" under RA 6713 is the transfer of title or disposal of interest in property in favor of a person other than:
choices: a foreign national or foreign firm
explanation: Section 3(j) requires divestment to be in favor of a person or persons other than the official's spouse and relatives; transferring to them does not count.
quote: in favor of a person or persons other than his spouse and relatives as defined in this Act

stem: Which norm of conduct under RA 6713 requires officials to use government resources efficiently, effectively, honestly and economically to avoid wastage of public funds?
explanation: Under Section 4(A)(a), commitment to public interest includes using government resources and powers efficiently, effectively, honestly and economically, particularly to avoid wastage in public funds and revenues.
quote: All government resources and powers of their respective offices must be employed and used efficiently, effectively, honestly and economically, particularly to avoid wastage in public funds and revenues.

stem: Which norm of conduct requires public officials to perform their duties with the highest degree of excellence, intelligence and skill?
explanation: Section 4(A)(b), Professionalism, requires performing duties with the highest degree of excellence, professionalism, intelligence and skill.
quote: Public officials and employees shall perform and discharge their duties with the highest degree of excellence, professionalism, intelligence and skill.

stem: Under the norm of justness and sincerity, officials shall not discriminate against anyone, especially:
explanation: Section 4(A)(c) requires officials to act with justness and sincerity and not discriminate against anyone, especially the poor and the underprivileged.
quote: shall not discriminate against anyone, especially the poor and the underprivileged

stem: Under RA 6713, officials may extend favors to relatives on account of their office ONLY with respect to appointments to positions that are:
choices: strictly confidential or personal staff coterminous with the official
in the same agency but under a different department head
highly technical and vacant for more than six months
in the career service that require civil service eligibility
explanation: Section 4(A)(c) bars undue favors to relatives, except appointments to positions considered strictly confidential or as members of personal staff whose terms are coterminous with the official's.
quote: except with respect to appointments of such relatives to positions considered strictly confidential or as members of their personal staff whose terms are coterminous with theirs

stem: A government clerk serves all clients equally regardless of the clients' party affiliation. This reflects which norm of conduct?
explanation: Section 4(A)(d), Political neutrality, requires service to everyone without unfair discrimination and regardless of party affiliation or preference.
quote: Public officials and employees shall provide service to everyone without unfair discrimination and regardless of party affiliation or preference.

stem: Extending prompt, courteous, and adequate service to the public and avoiding red tape falls under which norm of conduct?
explanation: Section 4(A)(e), Responsiveness to the public, requires prompt, courteous, and adequate service, openness of information, and avoiding red tape.
quote: Public officials and employees shall extend prompt, courteous, and adequate service to the public.

stem: Promoting the use of locally produced goods, resources and technology is part of which norm of conduct?
explanation: Under Section 4(A)(f), Nationalism and patriotism includes loyalty to the Republic and promoting the use of locally produced goods, resources and technology.
quote: promote the use of locally produced goods, resources and technology

stem: Under the norm of commitment to democracy, public officials shall put loyalty to country above loyalty to:
explanation: Section 4(A)(g) requires officials to uphold the Constitution and put loyalty to country above loyalty to persons or party.
quote: put loyalty to country above loyalty to persons or party

stem: A public employee who avoids extravagant or ostentatious display of wealth is observing which norm of conduct?
explanation: Section 4(A)(h), Simple living, requires officials and their families to lead modest lives and not indulge in extravagant or ostentatious display of wealth.
quote: They shall not indulge in extravagant or ostentatious display of wealth in any form.

stem: Under RA 6713, within how many working days must public officials respond to letters and other communications sent by the public?
explanation: Section 5(a) requires a response within fifteen (15) working days from receipt, and the reply must contain the action taken on the request.
quote: within fifteen (15) working days from receipt thereof, respond to letters, telegrams or other means of communications sent by the public

stem: Heads of government offices must render an annual performance report within how many working days from the end of the year?
explanation: Section 5(b) requires heads of offices and agencies to render a performance report within forty-five (45) working days from the end of the year.
quote: within forty-five (45) working days from the end of the year, render a performance report

stem: As far as practicable, official papers and documents should contain not more than how many signatories?
explanation: Section 5(c) states that official documents must contain, as far as practicable, not more than three (3) signatories.
quote: not more than three (3) signatories therein

stem: Who co-chair the Committee on Awards to Outstanding Public Officials and Employees under RA 6713?
choices: The President and the Senate President
The Ombudsman and the Chairman of the Civil Service Commission
The Chief Justice and the Ombudsman
The Chairman of the Commission on Audit and the Executive Secretary
explanation: Section 6 creates the Committee with the Ombudsman and the CSC Chairman as Co-Chairmen, and the COA Chairman and two presidential appointees as members.
quote: the Ombudsman and Chairman of the Civil Service Commission as Co-Chairmen

stem: Under RA 6713, public officials shall not have any financial or material interest in any transaction:
choices: requiring the approval of their office
explanation: Section 7(a) prohibits any direct or indirect financial or material interest in any transaction requiring the approval of their office.
quote: Public officials and employees shall not, directly or indirectly, have any financial or material interest in any transaction requiring the approval of their office.

stem: The prohibitions on outside employment under Section 7(b) of RA 6713 continue to apply for how long after resignation, retirement, or separation from office?
explanation: Section 7(b) extends these prohibitions for a period of one (1) year after resignation, retirement, or separation from public office.
quote: These prohibitions shall continue to apply for a period of one (1) year after resignation, retirement, or separation from public office

stem: Which of the following is a prohibited act under Section 7(b) of RA 6713?
choices: Owning a home in the province
Recommending a person to a private company that has a pending transaction with one's office
Attending a public seminar on ethics
Teaching part-time with the agency head's permission where allowed by law
explanation: Section 7(b)(3) prohibits recommending any person to any position in a private enterprise which has a regular or pending official transaction with the official's office.
quote: Recommend any person to any position in a private enterprise which has a regular or pending official transaction with their office.

stem: Using confidential information known by reason of one's office to give undue advantage to anyone is prohibited under RA 6713 as:
choices: disclosure and/or misuse of confidential information
explanation: Section 7(c) prohibits using or divulging confidential or classified information officially known by reason of office to further private interests, give undue advantage to anyone, or prejudice the public interest.
quote: To further their private interests, or give undue advantage to anyone

stem: Regarding gifts from foreign governments, Congress consents to a public official's acceptance of all of the following EXCEPT:
choices: Travel grants for travel entirely outside the Philippines, if permitted by the head of office
A scholarship or fellowship grant or medical treatment
A gift of nominal value received as a souvenir or mark of courtesy
Cash gifts of any amount given as tokens of friendship
explanation: Section 7(d) lists only the three consented cases: nominal-value souvenirs, scholarship/fellowship grants or medical treatment, and appropriate travel grants outside the Philippines permitted by the head of office.

stem: Who among the following is NOT required to file a Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALN) under RA 6713?
explanation: Section 8(A) exempts those who serve in an honorary capacity, laborers, and casual or temporary workers.
quote: All public officials and employees, except those who serve in an honorary capacity, laborers and casual or temporary workers, shall file under oath their Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth

stem: After the first filing, the SALN must be filed on or before what date every year?
explanation: Section 8(A) requires filing within thirty days after assumption of office, on or before April 30 of every year thereafter, and within thirty days after separation from the service.
quote: on or before April 30, of every year thereafter

stem: A newly appointed employee must file their SALN within how many days after assumption of office?
explanation: Section 8(A) requires the SALN to be filed within thirty (30) days after assumption of office.
quote: within thirty (30) days after assumption of office

stem: Husband and wife who are both public employees may file their SALN:
choices: only through the head of office
explanation: Section 8(A) provides that husband and wife who are both public officials or employees may file the required statements jointly or separately.
quote: Husband and wife who are both public officials or employees may file the required statements jointly or separately.

stem: Under RA 6713, how long must statements filed under the Act be available to the public?
explanation: Section 8(C)(4) keeps statements available to the public for ten (10) years after receipt, after which they may be destroyed unless needed in an ongoing investigation.
quote: Any statement filed under this Act shall be available to the public for a period of ten (10) years after receipt of the statement.

stem: When a conflict of interest arises, an official must divest themselves of shareholdings or interest within how many days from assumption of office?
explanation: Section 9 requires resigning from the private business within thirty (30) days and/or divesting shareholdings or interest within sixty (60) days from assumption of office.
quote: divest himself of his shareholdings or interest within sixty (60) days from such assumption

stem: Violations of Sections 7, 8 or 9 of RA 6713 are punishable by imprisonment not exceeding:
explanation: Section 11(a) punishes violations of Sections 7, 8 or 9 with imprisonment not exceeding five (5) years, a fine not exceeding ₱5,000, or both, plus possible disqualification from public office.
quote: Violations of Sections 7, 8 or 9 of this Act shall be punishable with imprisonment not exceeding five (5) years

stem: Which agency has the primary responsibility for the administration and enforcement of RA 6713?
explanation: Section 12 gives the Civil Service Commission the primary responsibility for the administration and enforcement of the Act.
quote: The Civil Service Commission shall have the primary responsibility for the administration and enforcement of this Act.

stem: Under RA 6713, a violation proven in a proper administrative proceeding is sufficient cause for removal or dismissal:
choices: even if no criminal prosecution is instituted
only if the official is elected
explanation: Section 11(b) makes an administratively proven violation sufficient cause for removal or dismissal even if no criminal prosecution is instituted.
quote: Any violation hereof proven in a proper administrative proceeding shall be sufficient cause for removal or dismissal of a public official or employee, even if no criminal prosecution is instituted against him.
